## 1. The people of Tubba'  (`#the-people-of-tubba`)

Cited ayat: 44:37, 50:14

> **44:37** أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ مُجْرِمِينَ

> **50:14** وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ

### Claims

**c1** (44:37): The Quran asks whether those addressed are better than the people of Tubba' and those before them.

**c2** (44:37): The ayah says that God destroyed them, because they were criminals.

**c3** (50:14): Another passage names the people of Tubba' in a list of peoples who denied the messengers.

**c4** (50:14): The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due.

### One-minute summary

The Quran asks whether those addressed are better than the people of Tubba' and says that God destroyed them because they were criminals [c1][c2]. It also names them among peoples who denied the messengers [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The Quran asks whether those addressed are better than the people of Tubba' and those before them [c1]. The ayah says that God destroyed them, because they were criminals [c2]. Another passage names the people of Tubba' in a list of peoples who denied the messengers [c3]. The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due [c4].

### Deep study

- The Quran asks whether those addressed are better than the people of Tubba' and those before them (44:37) [c1].
- The ayah says that God destroyed them, because they were criminals (44:37) [c2].
- Another passage names the people of Tubba' in a list of peoples who denied the messengers (50:14) [c3].
- The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due (50:14) [c4].

### Kids mode

The Quran mentions the people of Tubba' and says that God destroyed them, because they were criminals [c1][c2]. It also names them with other peoples who did not believe the messengers [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The first ayah addresses its hearers with a comparison and a reminder of an earlier people [c1][c2]. One reading is that the ayat use the people of Tubba' as one example among others of the end of those who deny [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who Tubba' was, whether the word is a name or a title, whether it names a king, where or when the people lived, or what they did; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the draft does not say who is addressed in 44:37 beyond the ayah's own words.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of Tubba' with a king or dynasty, a country or a date; none is used here.
